item.title: Ice Cube & Mike Epps Bring Dr. Dre To The Porch In “Listen & Laugh” Trailer
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Ice Cube and Mike Epps previewed Dr. Dre, Regina King and more guests in the official trailer for their "Listen & Laugh" podcast.
item.content:encoded:
Ice Cube laid out an informal approach for his “Listen & Laugh” podcast with Mike Epps in the official trailer: “We ain’t no pro podcasters, so we gonna do this shit our way.”

The three-minute official “Listen & Laugh” trailer previews a show that puts the two longtime friends in conversations about music, movies, comedy and sports.

The announced “Listen & Laugh” schedule called for new episodes on Fridays at 6 P.M. Eastern and 3 P.M. Pacific, with full conversations on YouTube and audio through podcast platforms. A full-episode premiere date had not been announced.

The teased guests included Dr. Dre, T.I., The Game, Regina King, Bill Burr, Stephen A. Smith and Lil Dicky, along with Cedric the Entertainer, Dana White, Michael Blackson, Funny Marco and O’Shea Jackson Jr.

During Dre’s appearance, Epps turned the producer’s work with Eminem into a joke. Guests also used Cube’s gangster-rap image as material, and Epps set up another exchange by identifying the set as the original “Friday” porch. Cube corrected him.

King played Cube’s sister, Dana, in the original “Friday.” Cube and Epps played Craig Jones and Day-Day in “Next Friday” in 2000, then reunited for “Friday After Next” in 2002.

The podcast gave the pair another chance to collaborate as “Last Friday” moved toward production.

They submitted the movie’s script in July, and Lawrence Lamont, who directed Keke Palmer and SZA in “One Of Them Days,” was named its director in October. California also selected the film for production tax credits on October 7, with Cube identified as its star, writer and producer.

“I’m thrilled to produce Last Friday right here in Southern California, where our cast and crew lives,” Cube said in the state announcement.

The production planned to employ more than 180 local cast and crew members.

The publisher’s description also put personal stories on the table, from first crushes and heartbreak to career breaks.

It described the hosts’ roles this way: “Cube’s gonna make you listen and Epps is gonna make you laugh. And sometimes, it will be the other way around.” The description named “Last Friday” among the subjects the hosts would discuss.

item.title: Vic Mensa Says He’s Taking Himself Seriously As A Producer On Next Album
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Vic Mensa described a new approach to his next album as his Chicago homecoming put longtime musical ties back onstage.
item.content:encoded:
Vic Mensa said he was taking himself seriously as a producer on his next album.

“It’s the first album that I’ve really taken myself completely seriously as a producer,” he said in The Verge interview.

The Chicago rapper named Apple’s Voice Memos his go-to tool for saving songs and other ideas. “Everything starts there for me.”

That next record already has a business plan behind it. UnitedMasters announced its partnership with Mensa in September, with a new full-length album set for 2027. The company put the return of Innanetape first on its release schedule, bringing the 2013 mixtape to streaming services on September 30.

The deal also included plans for live shows.

It followed sundiata, which Mensa had released independently through his own website in June. UnitedMasters described a partnership that would support his work in music, film, media and commerce while keeping ownership with the artist.

Fans in his hometown got a look back at the music that helped build that career just days before the interview was published. Mensa played Garcia’s Chicago in the West Loop on October 28 as part of his four-city “Innane Tour.”

Chance The Rapper joined him for “Suitcase,” a bonus track on the streaming edition of Innanetape and Joey Purp opened the show. The lineup brought longtime collaborators into the same small room as Mensa revisited the project 13 years after its release.

His work outside records has grown this year, too.

“The Vic Mensa Show” was announced in August with 24 episodes planned for its first season and Chance booked for the premiere. Rapsody, Lena Waithe and Aja Monet were among the announced guests.

“Music, culture and politics have always been intrinsically intertwined in my practice and in the larger tradition from which I emerge,” Mensa told Billboard about the show.

The series paired Mass Appeal with ORANJ, Mensa’s production company. Pickup Media and Blank Square Productions joined him as executive producers, with distribution planned across Spotify, Apple and YouTube.

item.title: The Neighborhood Kids Explain Why Rap And Resistance Belong Together
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: The Neighborhood Kids explained why protest belongs in Hip-Hop after bringing their message to Tom Morello's festival.
item.content:encoded:
The Neighborhood Kids made their case for protest rap in a new interview. Amon the MC argued that music born from struggle should speak to it.

“Hip Hop was birthed in the struggle,” Amon told Daylight. The San Diego rapper said the genre’s origins made it a natural tool for speaking about oppression.

“It was birthed by oppressed people, so it only makes sense that people should use it to talk about the oppression of the people. I think to use such a powerful art form and talk about nonsense is just blasphemous to me,” Amon the MC said.

For fellow MC Verde, the motivation was empathy. She said she wanted to make room for people whose suffering might otherwise go unheard. The bilingual group pairs the two rappers with DJ JG and live musicians.

That mission had a fitting setting on October 3, when Tom Morello introduced the group to open his “Power To The People” festival at Merriweather Post Pavilion in Columbia, Maryland. A Rogers Revue eyewitness account described a four-song set on the Chrysalis stage. Amon led the crowd in a call-and-response. The group closed with “Kids in the Cages.”

The event also gave fans places to act on what they heard. Its Freedom Village hosted nonprofit groups including Rock the Vote and the National Domestic Workers Alliance.

The group had already shared a bill with Morello at his “Defend L.A.” protest fundraiser in Los Angeles in June 2025.

Morello’s ties to outspoken rappers go back decades. When Ice-T inducted Rage Against the Machine into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2023, he recalled how the band landed an early opening slot for Body Count.

The festival followed another stop outside the group’s hometown: a June 2026 session for “Live on KEXP”. The station’s episode credits listed Amon and Verde on vocals alongside DJ JG. KEXP published the five-song session on its podcast in August.

Their message was already clear in an April 2026 interview with Jejune.

Amon explained that a song could reach someone who would never sit through a speech. Verde pointed to the way listeners learn songs and keep them in their lives. Amon also described different sounds for their full-band and three-piece sets, while stressing that both carried the same intensity.

Looking back on the October festival, Amon told Daylight, “It felt beautiful seeing so many people come out for love, resistance and music.”

item.title: Erick the Architect Embraces Improvisation On “AFTERBURNER”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Erick the Architect used more improvisation on Afterburner, building much of his next album in the order listeners will hear it.
item.content:encoded:
Erick the Architect made much of AFTERBURNER by improvising in the booth, changing a routine that once meant writing every line first.

Most sessions took place in 2025 and followed the eventual track order. At times, he recorded with his eyes closed. Prince and D’Angelo helped shape his plan for music that flowed from one track into the next.

That approach differs from how the Flatbush Zombies member put together his 2024 debut, I’ve Never Been Here Before.

He explained that the record brought new songs together with material recorded five years earlier.

“When I first started making this album, it took so many different forms in my mind after my debut, I promised myself that things had to be different this time around. This album is music in propulsion momentum. As philosophy it’s a testament to how far creativity can stretch in a time when so much of what we hear and see every day feels mundane and boring as fuck,” Erick the Architect explained.

His older songs were part of a plan, too. Speaking with Brooklyn Magazine about that debut, he said he held some records until he found the right music to place around them.

He also recalled a listener who only understood “Parkour” after hearing where it fit on the album.

“But I made an album. I didn’t make a bunch of singles,” he told Brooklyn Magazine.

He wanted listeners who already knew him to hear what else he could do as a solo artist.

AllHipHop covered “Instincts” with Westside Boogie during that rollout, which also included plans for his first major solo tour.

Working with other producers had already changed his role in the studio.

In the Brooklyn Magazine interview, Erick credited T-Minus, Linden Jay and James Blake with helping his writing. He still worked on arrangements and brought musicians into the process, rather than playing everything himself.

He had also described writing “Ezekiel’s Wheel” quickly, in a way that felt like a stream of consciousness. That was his account of writing a song for the debut.

The new announcement describes improvisation during recording across much of the next album.

AFTERBURNER, his second solo album and first full-length for Mass Appeal is due January 22, 2027.

item.title: Blxckie Reveals The Tour Lesson Bas Taught Him
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Blxckie said Bas taught him to record on tour as he discussed A-Reece, younger artists and the work behind his new album YENA.
item.content:encoded:
Blxckie said Bas taught him to treat the road as a studio, keeping his gear close so new experiences could become songs right away.

Speaking on Apple Music’s Africa Now Radio, the South African rapper recalled recording at venues while touring with Bas. He also learned how to stay in touch with fans while moving from place to place.

“There’s stuff that happens on tour that maybe you feel like you gotta get on record ASAP,” Blxckie said.

He also described a two-way exchange, with the chance to show Bas the scene back home in South Africa.

That U.S. run included a final stop at New York’s Irving Plaza on April 9, 2024. Blxckie opened the show alongside Reuben Vincent and Hoosh, with each getting roughly 20 minutes onstage.

Bas performed songs from We Only Talk About Real Shit When We’re Fucked Up, the album behind that tour, alongside older material. Bas also told the crowd about first hearing Blxckie’s music in South Africa.

Blxckie also pointed to A-Reece as someone he studied, especially his independence and connection with fans. He said he wanted to perform with a band, too.

Both rappers joined him on YENA, the 15-track album released October 30 through Somnyama Music Entertainment and EMPIRE. Bas appeared on “cover me,” while A-Reece joined “bonkerz.”

The tracklist also paired Blxckie with Nigerian singer L.A.X on “lonely,” KindlyNxsh on “let em have it” and Usimamane on “dradi.” It opened with “mama, it’s all good” and included “brady’s interlude.”

The production credits stretched from KindlyNxsh to American producer TM88. Blxckie had also released the 4LUV2 EP earlier this year before moving on to the full-length album.

Blxckie said younger artists inspired him by putting their cultures into their sound. He singled out KindlyNxsh’s Shona identity and K1llbrady’s approach as examples. For his own music, he said success now meant telling the stories he wanted to tell without outside influence.

item.title: Xaviersobased Explains How He Kept Release Freedom In Atlantic Deal
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Xaviersobased detailed a two-project Atlantic arrangement that let him keep releasing singles and videos outside the label.
item.content:encoded:
Xaviersobased signed with Atlantic Records without giving up his ability to put out singles and videos on his own, according to a newly published account of his deal.

In an interview with Hypebeast, the New York rapper and his manager, DJ Rennessy, explained why they waited before joining a major. He signed in 2025. The interview took place in late August and was published October 28.

“In the beginning we were definitely avoiding the labels, the majors. Because we knew we didn’t have that leverage,” he said.

The arrangement covered two projects through O1-chance, Surf Gang and Atlantic, Hypebeast reported. It also let him release singles and videos independently. His manager said the team pushed to keep that freedom rather than rush into a deal.

That concern about control had come up earlier this year. In The FADER’s February profile, Xavier was surprised to learn that Atlantic had sent the writer an advance stream of his album. He said he wanted to be told when his music was shared.

“I like to know what my music is doing,” he said.

The same profile traced how he taught himself to make beats and record. Bigger shows had also changed how he thought about his recordings. Some older tracks were hard to perform because of their sound quality. He wanted to improve that sound while still trying new ideas, not abandon his experiments.

A September arena booking put him on the same bill as Ken Carson. Barclays Center listed Xaviersobased, Prettifun and DJ Moon for the September 3 show.

Speaking with Teen Vogue the day after his performance at Barclays Center, he described meeting different crowds on their terms, whether they wanted to dance or rage. He was also still adjusting to studio work after making music at his grandmother’s home.

He said New York audiences felt especially close to him, including young Spanish fans who saw themselves in him.

His goal was to bring his musical and visual ideas to life more fully. Success, he told the magazine, meant being able to keep supporting himself for the rest of his life.

item.title: Jodeci Moves Ontario Anniversary Show From October To January
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jodeci moved its Toyota Arena anniversary show from October 27 to January 16, with Eric Bellinger also on the bill.
item.content:encoded:
Jodeci fans will have to wait until next year for the group’s Ontario, California anniversary show. The concert had been set for October 27.

The Toyota Arena concert has moved to Saturday, January 16, 2027. The Ticketmaster event page confirms the switch from October 27, 2026, to the new January date.

Eric Bellinger is also on the bill. Toyota Arena lists an 8 P.M. show, with doors opening at 7 P.M. The venue remains the same, at 4000 East Ontario Center Parkway.

The stop is part of Jodeci’s “35th Anniversary Tour Of Forever My Lady.” The tour marks 35 years since the group’s 1991 debut album. Neither the venue’s event page nor Ticketmaster’s listing explains the date change.

For fans who already bought tickets, Ticketmaster’s rescheduling guidance says they remain valid for the new date. That includes purchased upgrades and add-ons such as parking. Fans who bought at a venue box office are directed to that box office for more details.

The Ontario listing also includes an all-sales-final notice stating there are no refunds or exchanges. Ticketmaster’s general policy leaves refund options to event organizers on a show-by-show basis. Ticket holders who cannot attend in January should check their order information for any options attached to their purchase.

The anniversary puts Forever My Lady back at the center of Jodeci’s live plans. The album introduced songs including “Forever My Lady,” “Stay,” and “Come & Talk To Me.” It later earned a triple-platinum certification from the RIAA.

The group has made other live plans around its catalog in recent years.

As AllHipHop previously reported, DeVanté Swing, Mr. Dalvin, K-Ci and JoJo announced a Las Vegas residency with runs set for March and July 2024. The venue was House of Blues inside Mandalay Bay.

The booking drew its name from their 1995 album The Show, the After Party, the Hotel.

The group’s official tour schedule now places Ontario within a January run through the West. San Francisco is set for January 8, followed by Inglewood on January 9 and El Cajon on January 10. Phoenix is listed for January 15. Toyota Arena comes next, ahead of a January 17 booking in Las Vegas.

item.title: TOB’s Lil Chris Says Chief Keef Didn’t Cause “Shake That” Streaming Removal
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: TOB's Lil Chris denied Chief Keef caused the "Shake That" takedown and alleged a false complaint pulled the viral go-go record.
item.content:encoded:
TOB’s Lil Chris said Chief Keef and his team were not behind the streaming removal of “Shake That (I Just Wanna Dance).”

Speaking with Aladdin Da Prince on 93.9 WKYS, Chris alleged that a false complaint caused the takedown. He also said Keef publicly supported the record.

The disruption followed a breakthrough for the go-go band. A Nucci’s Front Porch performance helped the song take off before Queen Peachifi’s dance carried it across TikTok.

Chris described TOB’s recent run as a “second half comeback” and said its audience extended to Poland, Tokyo and the United Kingdom. He said it was connecting young listeners with longtime go-go fans.

Getting go-go heard beyond Washington has long involved more than making a record people love. In a 2020 exclusive AllHipHop interview, DJ Kool pointed to the promotional support behind hits as one reason the genre had not enjoyed Hip-Hop’s wider commercial reach.

“We never got the proper marketing that Hip-Hop has got,” he said.

He used E.U.’s “Da Butt” as an example, crediting the machinery around the song and its connection to Spike Lee. The discussion accompanied TV One’s documentary “The Beat Don’t Stop,” which featured TOB alongside acts including Trouble Funk and Junk Yard Band.

DJ Kool also stressed recording during that earlier interview, saying “but it’s up to the group’s to get into the studio and make original material.”

A recent release offered another example of how go-go performances can move onto bigger distribution platforms.

Tone P’s “Tha Carry Out” recorded and executive produced Nino Paid’s live version of “Shine” with Hvmane Studios. Signal/Columbia Records acquired and released it, making it the platform’s first major-label release across streaming services.

The series turns familiar songs into go-go performances and has featured TOB among its guests.

That separate release put the live format into a label-backed rollout, while TOB’s current situation centers on getting its own viral record back to listeners.

At WKYS, Chris premiered an exclusive, newly recorded studio version of “Shake That (I Just Wanna Dance).” He announced plans to restore the song to streaming and said TOB had more original music planned for 2027.

item.title: 85 South Media Lands Tubi Distribution Deal
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: 85 South Media signed a Tubi distribution deal for a 10-episode collection featuring DC Young Fly, Karlous Miller and Chico Bean.
item.content:encoded:
Atlanta-based 85 South Media signed a Tubi distribution deal that will bring 10 episodes of “The 85 South Show” to the free streamer, according to Deadline.

The collection, “The Best Of The 85 South Show,” features DC Young Fly, Karlous Miller and Chico Bean. More programming is expected, though those projects have not been named.

Chad Oubre, the company’s CEO and co-founder, told Deadline the expansion would help 85 South reach more viewers as it continued to build its own business.

The comedians already had a movie in Tubi’s plans. On October 29, 2025, the company announced a four-film deal with Kevin Hart’s Hartbeat, including “85 South: Dead End.” The horror comedy follows the trio on a road trip through the South that leads them to a town people cannot leave.

That slate also included “Sundown,” a supernatural thriller written and directed by Kinigra Deon, who starred in it. Tubi placed both projects under its Tubi for Creators program, a push to bring creators’ work to the service and give them a wider audience.

DC Young Fly and Miller had another Tubi connection through T.I.’s “Da Partments”.

AllHipHop reported in 2023 that DC co-produced the Atlanta comedy while Miller and Lil Duval served as executive producers. All three appeared in the film, which T.I. wrote and directed.

The trio’s reach extended beyond their podcast. Netflix released their stand-up special “85 South: Ghetto Legends” in 2023.

It brought the same three comedians together for a stage show built around their podcast’s freewheeling comedy.

Their work also earned recognition at the 2024 NAACP Image Awards, where “The 85 South Show” won Outstanding Society and Culture Podcast. DC separately won the hosting award for “Celebrity Squares,” while “Wild ‘n Out,” which featured all three comics, won its reality program category.

Fans can also find the crew on Channel Eighty Five, their own subscription streaming service. Its catalog includes their classic shows and original series, with Desi Banks, Moneybag Mafia and Navv Greene among the featured comics. The service advertises its live-show library as an exclusive part of that offering and lists a monthly price of $8.50.

item.title: Learjet Crash Killed Nine As Jet Nosedives Into Florida Neighborhood
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.category: signs the world is coming to an end
item.description: Learjet disaster prompted a federal inquiry after a Caribbean itinerary became a deadly aviation emergency amid suburban streets.
item.content:encoded:
A Learjet traveling to the Bahamas ended in tragedy Sunday when the jet carrying nine people crashed near Florida homes and killed everyone aboard.

The Learjet 60 went down in a residential area near Cresthaven in Palm Beach County at approximately 12:50 p.m. Nov. 1, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed that all nine occupants died.

The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was traveling to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. Its flight ended near Military Trail, where emergency crews responded to flames and wreckage beside a residential community.

Video showed the jet descending steeply before exploding near a roadway. The impact left a burning crater and sent thick black smoke above the surrounding neighborhood. Homes and passing vehicles were close to where the aircraft struck, according to reporting by The Associated Press.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of people on the ground being injured or killed. Officials had not identified the nine occupants or released a breakdown of passengers and crew in the reporting reviewed for this story.

The emergency response disrupted traffic along Military Trail between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North. Palm Beach County sheriff’s deputies closed the roadway in both directions and asked motorists to avoid the area as authorities worked at the scene. Florida Power & Light crews also responded.

Federal investigators will now determine what caused the fatal descent. The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board are investigating, with the NTSB directing the inquiry and providing subsequent updates. The FAA cautioned that its initial information was preliminary and subject to change.

The NTSB said investigators would arrive Sunday and Monday, according to CNN. A Monday news conference was also planned. No cause had been established in the reports reviewed.

A flight intended to connect Texas with the Bahamas instead ended beside Florida homes. Nine people were killed, a neighborhood became an emergency scene and the explanation for the aircraft’s final descent remained unresolved.
